//: parts.json -- THE partition of Fizzygum's shipped source into a core plus named PARTS.
WHAT A PART IS. A named slice of the system that can be included or excluded as a unit, and
(from arc 4 phase 2) loaded at boot or on demand. Every directory that ships appears in
EXACTLY ONE part; a .coffee file under src/ that no part claims is a BUILD FAILURE
(buildSystem/check-shippable-coverage.js). That is stronger than what came before: build.py
used to carry a hand-maintained sequence of glob('src/<dir>/*.coffee') calls, and a new
directory that nobody remembered to add there shipped as NOTHING -- the build stayed green and
the only symptom was a runtime '<NewClass> is not defined'.
WHAT REPLACED WHAT (arc 4 phase 1). Part membership is what the whole-file marker
'# this file is excluded from the fizzygum homepage build' used to say, one file at a time, in
45 files, read by three regexes in build.py. Those are all gone. Exclusion is now a property of
a NAMED SLICE, stated once -- rather than an invisible property of a file you only discover by
opening it.
WHERE INCLUSION LIVES (arc 5): NOT here. A part is in an artifact because the PROFILE being
built names it -- buildSystem/profiles/<name>.json, read by buildSystem/buildProfile.py. This
file is the partition (what the parts ARE and what they own); a profile is the flavour (which of
them ship). The 'inHomepage' boolean that used to sit on each part below was inclusion for the
ONE hard-coded flavour, and it is gone: 'which parts does production have?' is answered by
reading profiles/homepage.json, not by grepping eleven booleans.
INCLUSION AND TIMING ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES (do not conflate them -- arc 4 reframe R6):
inclusion is a profile's business (above); `eager` here is TIMING -- loaded at boot, or on
demand? A marker could only ever express the first. Keeping them separate is what let arc 4
change inclusion with provably zero runtime change, leaving timing to its next phase.
FIELDS
dirs         directories whose *.coffee files belong to this part. Not recursive: list each.
eager        default true. false = loaded on demand (needs a launch site that awaits
world.parts.ensureLoaded, NOT a bare `if TheClass?` guard).
requiresFlag optional build flag this part additionally needs, on TOP of being selected by the
profile. One carrier left ('videoPlayer'): a per-invocation opt-in rather than a
property of an artifact. ('tests' is gone -- whether the test machinery ships is
now just whether a profile selects the harness part, so it is not asked twice.)
bootPrelude  optional src/boot/*.coffee pieces concatenated into the boot bundle when this part
ships. Not part sources (those are classes, wrapped as text and compiled in the
browser): these are prototype extensions the bundle needs before any class runs.
numbertimes.coffee is the one carrier -- it extends Number for the fizzytiles LCL
preprocessor, and it used to be appended under `if ! $homepage`, i.e. the build
script knew a fact about a part.
vendor       optional non-source payloads that must arrive with the part, each
{ out: <path relative to the build root>, concat: [<pieces relative to
Fizzygum/>] }. build.py ASSEMBLES each one (pieces joined by a newline-semicolon
separator) for parts that ship, and emits only `out` into window.FIZZYGUM_PARTS,
because PartsRegistry consumes vendor entries as URLs to inject. Before arc 5
the fizzytiles payload was cat'd together by build_it_please.sh under `if the
vendored source file exists` -- no part or flavour test at all -- while its own
comment claimed 'emitted for every flavour that ships the part'. So a --homepage
tree carried 18.9 KB of software-3D engine for a part it does not ship.
assets       optional non-source FILES copied into the build tree for this part, as
[<path relative to Fizzygum/>, <destination dir relative to the build root>]
pairs. A part that does not ship copies none of them, which is how a flavour
stops shipping an asset with nobody maintaining a prune list. Arc 5 PR-D6:
the tail is DERIVED, never declared -- these pairs say who OWNS a file, and
what ships follows from that. The three pointer icons and FileSaver/JSZip used
to be copied unconditionally and then deleted again by the --homepage block.
So a part can own four kinds of thing -- sources (dirs), files (assets), assembled payloads
(vendor) and boot-bundle pieces (bootPrelude) -- and ALL FOUR appear or vanish together with the
part. That is the whole mechanism by which a flavour stops shipping something.
A part's absence must be a NO-OP at every call site, via the class-existence guard idiom
(`if DemoMenus?`, `world.pinouts?.reset()`, `WorldTestSupport.installOnto WorldWdgt if ...?`).
buildSystem/check-part-edges.js enforces that: an unguarded core reference to a part-owned
class fails the build.
CURRENT-STATE REFERENCE: docs/architecture/build-and-packaging.md -- the partition, the profiles,
and the full table of what a build DERIVES rather than declares. The arcs that produced this
shape: docs/archive/build-arc-4-dynamic-parts-plan.md (the partition) and
docs/archive/build-arc-5-packaging-profiles-plan.md (the profiles that select from it).

core.//: The product. Ships in every flavour, always eagerly. src/boot is absent on purpose: build_it_please.sh compiles those files BY NAME into the boot bundle, so they are not text-wrapped sources and not part material.
core.//dataflow: ⚠ src/dataflow IS CORE, DELIBERATELY -- do not extract it (owner decision, 2026-07-30). It looks like an app slice next to src/spreadsheet, and it is not: it is the wiring substrate every widget reaches (ControllerMixin.ensureWireEdge is how ANY widget wires to any other), and WorldWdgt.doOneCycle drains it EVERY cycle. Its 14 call sites are all already written `world.dataflow?.…`, so its absence would be silently ACCEPTED rather than caught -- wires would simply never fire, sliders would stop driving their targets, patch nodes would go dead. That is broken, not reduced, and it fails the absence-must-be-a-no-op rule below. Same judgment as src/meta.
core.//assets: The boot splash + spinner (drawn before any class exists) and the CoffeeScript compiler, which ships in EVERY profile: FizzyPaint tools, spreadsheet formulas, $src snapshot records and Fizzytiles' LCL are all compiled at runtime, so a compiler-less build is a non-interactive kiosk (arc 5 PR-D3).

meta-tools.//: The in-world INSPECTORS: InspectorWdgt, ClassInspectorWdgt (its subclass) and ConsoleWdgt. Split out of src/meta so that a lean/appliance profile can leave them out -- src/meta itself CANNOT become a part, because Class and Mixin live there and are the compile bootstrap. Production ships it (profiles/homepage.json names it) and always has; the `lean` profile is what drops it outright. Core reaches it through exactly two sites, Widget.spawnInspector and Widget.createConsole.
meta-tools.//eager: LAZY. An inspector is the definition of on-demand: nobody opens one during a normal session, and on a precompiled tree a lazy part's classes are absent from js/pre-compiled.js, so production stops paying for them up front. It pairs naturally with sources: "lazy" -- opening an inspector ALREADY had to await the reflective layer (an inspector reads class member maps, which exist only once the source text is ingested), so the part load joins an await that was there anyway. ⚠ The two call sites must NOT use `if InspectorWdgt?`: for a lazy part that reads 'not fetched yet' and swallows the click forever. They ask world.parts.isAvailable (did this artifact ship it at all) and then await.

fizzytiles.//: The Fizzytiles ('fridge magnets') engine: the tile widgets, the LiveCodeLang compiler/preprocessor/runner, and the SW3D output pane. THE LAZY PART -- the largest self-contained app in the tree, with a vendored 3D payload, reached from exactly two entry points. Its LAUNCHER is deliberately a separate, EAGER part (see fizzytiles-launcher) so the desktop icon exists before the engine does. 'eager: false' means index.html does not carry it until someone launches it; the harness and index-sw.html override that (FIZZYGUM_EAGER_ALL_PARTS) because a part arriving mid-test would be frame-paced and therefore cycle-count-dependent.
fizzytiles.//bootPrelude: Number::times / ::timesWithVariable, which the LiveCodeLang preprocessor emits for `3 times with i box`. It extends a built-in prototype, so it belongs in the boot bundle rather than among the part's classes -- but it exists ONLY for this part, and used to be appended by build_it_please.sh under `if ! $homepage`: a fact about a part, kept in the build script.

vendor.//: SWCanvas's subtractive 3D-CORE dist target (Surface + DepthBuffer + Texture3D + Triangle3DOps, ~14 KB vs ~263 KB for the full engine, pixel-identical on the 3D path) plus the minified SW3D userland engine. ⚠ The SW pages must NOT load this: their boot bundle carries the FULL SWCanvas as their renderer, so injecting the subtractive build over it would replace a superset with a subset. PartsRegistry's vendor step is idempotent and skips it when window.SW3D and SWCanvas.Core.Triangle3DOps are already present.

fizzytiles-launcher.//: The eager sliver of fizzytiles: the desktop launcher declaration plus its icon. It CANNOT be lazy -- WorldWdgt.createDesktop builds the desktop opener by instantiating FridgeMagnetsApp (and drawing FridgeMagnetsIconWdgt), and WellKnownObjects.resolveApp re-resolves snapshot references through the same class. An icon the user cannot see is an app they cannot launch. This is arc 4's reframe R6 in one part: INCLUSION and EAGERNESS are different properties, and 'the launcher is always here, the engine arrives when asked for' needs both.

demos.//: The demo/parts-bin catalogue (DemoMenus, reached as `demoMenus`) and the sample widgets it shows off: the bouncer, the pen, the pointer. Arc 3 extracted DemoMenus out of MenusHelper for exactly this; its own header already said 'arc 4 turns that into part membership'.
demos.//eager: LAZY. Nothing reaches the demo family until someone opens the 'demo ➜' or 'test menu ➜' entries, so it has no business compiling at boot -- 28 classes with src/demos-icons folded in. ⚠ Its doors are MENU ITEMS, which makes them a shape the app launchers do not have: a menu is BUILT synchronously (ButtonWdgt binds `@target[@action]` at build time), so the item cannot target the `demoMenus` singleton -- core owns the item, asks `world.parts.isAvailable "demos"` to decide whether to OFFER it, and awaits inside the action. See Widget.popUpDemoTestMenu. ⚠ Not shipped by any production profile, so this buys dev-page boot and partition uniformity, never download size.
demos.//icons: src/demos-icons holds the 23 icon classes ONLY DemoMenus names -- text-formatting glyphs (align/bold/italic/font-size/format-as-code), the collapsed/uncollapsed state pair, the little USA/world map glyphs, and the welcome/templates/text/video-play/C-F icons. They sat in src/icons, which is otherwise product, and are here for the same reason src/icons-dev exists: an icon belongs to whatever names it. ⚠ Their *IconAppearance siblings mostly did NOT come along -- 13 of them are named DIRECTLY by core toolbar buttons, so they stay in src/icons and this part reaches them the safe direction (part -> core, and core always ships). Only the five appearances whose sole namer was their own moving widget travelled with it.

plots.//: The plots/graphs family: AxisWdgt, PlotWithAxesWdgt, the four Example*Plot widgets and the 3D plot's little geometry kit (Point3D, Grid3D, PlaneGrid3D), plus the four creator buttons that make them, the PlotsToolbarWdgt palette and the button that pops it. 12 KB of code and ~19 KB of 3D scaffolding, none of it reachable until someone asks for a chart.
plots.//eager: LAZY, for the same reason as maps: production ships it (the sample dashboard, the sample slide and the sample doc all BUILD plots, so it cannot be dropped) but a lazy part's classes are absent from js/pre-compiled.js, so the first load does not carry it.
plots.//buttons: ⚠ The four creator buttons AND PlotsToolbarWdgt/PlotsToolbarCreatorButtonWdgt live here, not in core, and for two different reasons. The buttons: a creator button has no async seam (see the maps part), so it must sit in the part it creates from. The TOOLBAR: every one of its four items is a plot button, so a core toolbar filtering them out would open an EMPTY palette window -- worse than not offering it. Keeping the palette and its opener in the part means SuperToolbarWdgt filters ONE button and the palette is simply not offered until plots is in.

maps.//: The two vector maps -- SimpleUSAMapIconWdgt and SimpleWorldMapIconWdgt, each with its *Appearance -- and the two toolbar buttons that create them. 4 files but ~85 KB: the appearances are long vector-path artwork, which makes this the best bytes-per-edge slice in the tree and the least likely to be missed by a user who never opens it.
maps.//eager: LAZY, and production ships it that way: a lazy part's classes are NOT in js/pre-compiled.js (the image is harvested by booting index.html, where lazy parts by definition do not load), so profiles/homepage.json can keep the Examples AND not download the artwork until someone asks for a map.
maps.//buttons: ⚠ WHY THE TWO CREATOR BUTTONS LIVE HERE rather than with the other sample content. A creator button has NO async seam -- WidgetCreatorAndSmartPlacerOnClickMixin.mouseClickLeft and Widget.grabbedWidgetSwitcheroo both consume createWidgetToBeHandled()'s RETURN VALUE synchronously -- so a button outside this part could not await the load before constructing a map. Keeping the button in the part it creates from makes its mere EXISTENCE proof that its part is loaded, which is what turns an `if USAMapCreatorButtonWdgt?` filter in the core toolbars into a correct test instead of a swallowed click.

samples.//: The three EXAMPLE DOCUMENTS WorldWdgt.createDesktop drops into the desktop's 'Examples' folder -- SampleDashboardApp (plots + maps + sliders), SampleSlideApp (the NYC slide) and SampleDocApp. They are content, not product: each is an IconicDesktopSystemWindowedApp whose buildWindow assembles a finished document out of product widgets, to show what the system can do. They sat in core only because nothing had asked them to be separable; that is the same judgment arc 3 made for DemoMenus and arc 4 for the 'demos' part. ⚠ NOT folded INTO 'demos': production ships these (profiles/homepage.json names 'samples') and must NOT gain DemoMenus and the bouncer/pen/pointer, which is exactly what naming 'demos' there would do. Two separate species of demo, two parts. Core reaches them through the three guarded createOpener calls in createDesktop, so a profile without this part simply gets a smaller Examples folder.

spreadsheet.//: The spreadsheet ENGINE: the grid (SimpleSpreadsheetWdgt), its frame, the widgetised cells and headers with their appearances, the sparse SheetModel + SheetCellRecord, FormulaCompiler/FormulaHelpers and SheetError. 13 files, ~114 KB -- the largest app-like slice that was still sitting inside core. Its LAUNCHER is a separate, EAGER part (see spreadsheet-launcher), for the same reason fizzytiles has one: the desktop icon must exist before the engine does.
spreadsheet.//eager: LAZY, and production ships it that way (profiles/homepage.json names it): a lazy part's classes are absent from js/pre-compiled.js, so a visitor who never opens a sheet never pays for one. The one door is SpreadsheetApp.launch, which awaits.
spreadsheet.//dataflow: ⚠ THE ENGINE IT DEPENDS ON IS NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE. Cells are dataflow nodes, but src/dataflow stays in CORE -- it is the wiring substrate the whole system uses (ControllerMixin.ensureWireEdge, sliders, patch nodes, and WorldWdgt.doOneCycle's every-cycle drain), not an app slice, and its absence would be a silent semantic break rather than a no-op. So this part's door names ONE part, and the fact that parts.json has no part->part `requires` mechanism does not matter here. See docs/plans/core-app-slices-partition-plan.md §4 Phase 3 (amended) for the enumeration that settled it.

spreadsheet-launcher.//: The eager sliver of the spreadsheet: SpreadsheetApp, the desktop launcher declaration, and nothing else (its icon is built from core widgets, so unlike fizzytiles-launcher there is no icon file to bring along). It CANNOT be lazy -- WorldWdgt.createDesktop calls createOpener on it AT BOOT to place the Examples-folder icon, and WellKnownObjects.resolveApp re-resolves snapshot launcher references through the same class. Arc 4's reframe R6 again: INCLUSION and EAGERNESS are different properties, and 'the icon is always here, the grid arrives when asked for' needs both.
spreadsheet-launcher.//pairing: ⚠ A PROFILE SHOULD NAME BOTH PARTS OR NEITHER. This one alone would put a desktop icon on a tree whose click can only reject -- worse than no icon; the engine alone would ship 114 KB nothing can open. homepage names both, lean names neither.

dev-tools.//: In-world dev scaffolding: the widget factory (world.widgetFactory), the pinout debug overlay (world.pinouts, an arc-3 extraction), and the layout-editing chrome (spacers + the element adder/droplet) reached from the test menu. Every one of them is already an optional collaborator behind an existence guard.

dev-icons.//: The icon gallery the demo menus show: chapter markers, information, raster-pic, save, under-carpet. Moved out of the 159-file src/icons, which is otherwise all product.

patch-programming-experimental.//: The unfinished half of patch programming: fanout, diffing, regex-substitution nodes. src/patch-programming was a MIXED directory (PatchNodeWdgt and CalculatingPatchNodeWdgt ship, these six do not) and P-D2 resolves a mixed directory by MOVING files, never by tagging them.

macros.//: The macro engine + toolkit (world.macroToolkit): the authoring path for SystemTests. Test machinery that lives in src/ because the macros drive the product through its own API. Was excluded by the FILE_ONLY_FOR_MACROS marker regex; now by part.

harness.//: The Automator + test-harness sources, which live in the SIBLING TESTS REPO. Its five *TestSupport classes install themselves onto core prototypes at boot behind `if XTestSupport?`. ⚠ THIS PART IS WHAT MAKES A BUILD TEST-CAPABLE, so five derived facts key off its presence (buildProfile.py): the js/tests symlink, BUILDFLAG_LOAD_TESTS, the two tests-repo build gates, and -- inverted -- the strip of the dead `if Automator?` branches, since Automator/AutomatorLoader/AutomatorPlayer are all in here. It used to carry `requiresFlag: "tests"` on top of a flavour test, which asked the same question twice.
harness.//assets: The three pointer icons SystemTestsControlPanelUpdater sets as in the harness control panel (DOM, not canvas -- so no screenshot gate can see them go missing; the parts fingerprint is what checks them), plus FileSaver + JSZip, which globalFunctions only loads when BUILDFLAG_LOAD_TESTS is set and which product FileSaving.coffee explicitly does not depend on.

video-player.//: Already flag-gated before this arc; its whole-file marker was redundant belt-and-braces.
